Samir / Elena — thanks for the quick questions. See answers below and attached the short readout + configs we used. I kept the answers punchy so your infra team can skim.

1) p99 context: the p99=82ms figure reported in Ben's note was with the KV cache warming enabled (we ran a 20-minute warmup period before measurement). Cold-start p99 with cache cold is typically 180–220ms on the same hardware; tail smoothing requires either pre-warming or a hybrid fallback strategy.

2) FP16 -> 4-bit quantization: for the architecture we tested (decoder-only 7B variant), switching to 4-bit (we used q4_k_mixed) increased p50 by ~5–8ms in our runs but reduced token cost by ~35–40%. p99 impact depends on kernel maturity on the target GPU; for A100 the p99 delta was ~+10–15ms in our tests, but on Ampere/Infer class GPUs you might see larger variance. Recommendation: run a short quantized pass in your environment; we'll help automate that.

3) Batching mode: the runs used continuous batching with a 20–40ms batching window (adaptive) — that is, we keep a short queue to increase throughput without blowing up latency for steady-state. For purely on-demand single-request dispatch (no batching), you should expect ~30–40% higher per-token latency at similar throughput.

Retail burst guidance: for flash-burst patterns we typically suggest a two-tier approach — autoscale reserved capacity for steady-state + a short warm pool (dedicated burst nodes) with a policy for fast cold-start fallbacks (model smaller variant) during the first 2–3 minutes of a campaign spike. Details in the attached readout.

Attachments: redwood-latency-readout-20261110.pdf, test-configs-aws-k8s.csv
